chunks: It is narrated from ʿAmmār ibn Marwān al-Kalbī, who said:

Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام advised me and said: “I advise you to have taqwa of Allah, to render the trust, to speak truthfully, and to keep good companionship with whoever accompanies you, and ‘There is no power except by Allah.’”

key_terms.أَدَاءِ الْأَمَانَةِ: fulfilling and returning trusts owed to others
key_terms.بِتَقْوَى اللَّهِ: having God-consciousness and piety toward Allah
key_terms.لَا قُوَّةَ إِلَّا بِاللَّهِ: affirmation that all strength and power are only through Allah

ai.seo_question: What did Imam al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام advise regarding taqwa, trustworthiness, truthfulness, and companionship?
ai.summary: This hadith conveys a concise ethical counsel from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, centering on taqwa, fulfilling trusts, truthfulness, and good companionship. It concludes with the formula ‘There is no power except by Allah,’ linking moral conduct to reliance upon Allah.
